page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with 3780 GB of capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as average, multi-core performance is strong, supported by a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 89771.17. Memory subsystem performance shows strong read-only bandwidth at 332.26 GB/sec for large blocks, though write bandwidth is lower at 128.16 GB/sec. The processor's matrix extension capabilities contribute to top-tier prompt processing speeds in LLM inference, reaching 4079.59 tokens/sec for small models and 39.93 tokens/sec for large 70B models, though text generation speeds remain average.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of a substantial 3780 GB local disk, this server type provides high resource density for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads. It is suited for database operations, as reflected in its strong PassMark database score and Redis throughput of 117.01 million operations per second. The hardware configuration is also appropriate for static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration.
